mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing the discount rate for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.2% for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.5% signals a tightening labor market that increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 5.5%, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, boosting corporate profits and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving average, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 220) indicates a stable price environment, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain low interest rates and support positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL < 220, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 indicates expanding manufacturing and services, which increases corporate output and profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises above 100 but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 600,000 units signal a strong housing market that stimulates construction and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 600, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS) above 350,000 units indicate elevated consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS > 350000, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods.
